intro: Welcome to Earth Information Jukebox. Get ready to experience the world through sound! I'm Jodi, your personal guide, and I'll walk you through this journey using my voice. Every single note you hear from now on is data collected by NASA. You can experience five different maps audibly using this app: Ocean currents and sea surface temperature, Night lights, Lightning seen from the ISS, Aerosols, and Countries. Let me help you get started! Press Space to play or pause. Press E to explore a still frame with your keys, and Escape to leave explore. Press N and P to move forward and backward to find your preferred map. Press D to turn spoken descriptions on or off. Press G to switch between the globe and the flat map. You can use plus and minus to zoom in and out, and zero to reset. Press L to play the sound legend. Press M to turn on night mode. In explore, press one to choose the pointer. Keys two and three access row and column. Key four accesses a box, which covers a certain area. To move fast or resize the box, press shift with the arrow keys. Press A in the box tool to select the whole map. To step to the previous or next time frame, press the square brackets. If you missed any of these keys, don't worry: press H at any time to hear what all the keys do. You can press V to turn this voice guide off.
keys: Keys. Space: play or pause. N and P: next or previous visualization. E: explore the current frame. L: play the sound legend. D: spoken descriptions on or off. G: switch between the globe and the flat map. Plus and minus: zoom in and out, and zero to reset. M: night mode. V: voice guide on or off. K: speak a command. H: hear these keys again. In Explore: keys one to four choose Point, Row, Column or Box. Arrow keys move. Shift with an arrow moves faster, or resizes the box. Enter plays. I says where you are. A, in the Box tool, selects the whole map. The square brackets step to the previous or next frame. Escape leaves Explore.
explore: Explore. The picture is paused on one frame so you can study it. There are four tools. One, Point: a harp note plays the value under your probe, over a soft tone that glides with it. Higher means more, and silence means no data. Two, Row: a playhead sweeps from west to east, plucking the values as it goes, with a tick every thirty degrees. Three, Column: the same from north to south, with a deeper tick at the equator. Four, Box: scans an area from left to right, where north is higher and louder means more, then reads a summary. In the Box tool, A selects the whole map. Use the arrow keys to move and Enter to play. The square brackets step through time. Escape returns to playback.
ds-sst: Explore Ocean currents and sea surface temperature. The picture is paused on one frame now, so you can take your time and explore. Move your cursor across the screen and listen to how the ocean surface temperature sounds, using data from a NASA ocean model, March 2007 to March 2008. A low note {tone:low} means a cooler area of the ocean on average, and a high note {tone:high} means a warmer one. When more of the ocean is above twenty-eight degrees, the note repeats faster. Hotter hot spots make the sound louder and brighter. A soft bell marks each new month. Press Space to play, or E to explore a frame.
ds-nightlights: Explore Night Lights. The picture is paused on one frame now, so you can take your time and explore. Move your cursor across the screen and listen to how night lights seen from space, 2012 to 2023, sound. A low note {tone:low} means little of the map is lit, and a high note {tone:high} means much more is lit. More light also makes the note repeat faster. The years move from your left ear to your right. In the change map, a flute on the right means brighter, and a bass on the left means darker. Press Space to play, or E to explore.
ds-lightning: Explore Lightning. The picture is paused on one frame now, so you can take your time and explore. Move your cursor across the screen and listen to how lightning seen from the International Space Station sounds. A steady note underneath plays three times a second. It is low when storms are mostly in the south {tone:low}, and high when they are in the north. {tone:high} The louder the notes, the bigger the lightning strikes, so the rhythm you hear is the lightning itself. Press Space to play, or E to explore.
ds-earth: Explore Countries. Move your cursor across the screen and listen to how the distribution and geography of countries around the world sound, using NASA's Blue Marble, with country borders and real clouds. This is a still map for exploring, so it opens in Explore. Shallow seas sound like surf, and the deep ocean sounds like a low rumble that gets deeper with the water. On land, the sound is a warm tone that rises with height; high mountains add wind, and glaciers shimmer like ice. A soft tick means you crossed a border, and then the country name is spoken. Plus and minus zoom in to read the countries. Press Space to play, or E to explore.
ds-aerosols: Explore Aerosols: smoke, dust, sea salt and sulfate. Move your cursor across the screen and listen to how aerosols in the air around the whole planet, on one day in August 2025, sound. This is a still map for exploring, so it opens in Explore. A low tone {tone:low} means only a little aerosol in the air, and a high tone {tone:high} means a lot. Silence means clear air. When the type changes you hear a soft tick, and the new type is spoken. Choose the Box tool with key four, then press A to scan the whole map from west to east.
voice-help: Voice commands. Press K, then say a command. Play, pause, next, or previous. A visualization: ocean, night lights, lightning, aerosols, or Earth. Explore, and done. Point, row, column, box, whole map, and scan. North, south, east, or west, or far north. Next frame, and previous frame. Zoom in, zoom out, and reset zoom. Louder, quieter, faster, and slower. Legend, describe, night mode, and day mode. Where am I. And on the Earth map, go to a country, like go to France. Say repeat to hear the last message again.
